lyrics:
[Intro: bright electric guitar riff, driving drums]

[Verse 1: male voice, wry]
You got the couch and the good set of knives
I got the dog every other July
You kept the friends who could cook, I kept the ones who drink
We even split the airline miles, I think

[Pre-Chorus: female voice, wry]
But there's one thing left in the back of the van
Neither one of us wants in our hand

[Chorus: both voices, big guitars, handclaps]
So let's split the blame, right down the middle
I'll take the big half, you take the little
I wasn't a saint, you weren't a villain
We both held the match and we both did the spilling
Half's got your name and half's got my name
Come on, baby, split the blame

[Verse 2: female voice]
You shut down like a store on a Sunday
I picked fights on a perfectly good Monday
You never said sorry, I said it too mean
We were both pretty awful, somewhere in between

[Pre-Chorus: male voice]
Now we're two rows back at her graduation
Sharing a program and a parking situation

[Chorus: both voices, big guitars, handclaps]
So let's split the blame, right down the middle
I'll take the big half, you take the little
I wasn't a saint, you weren't a villain
We both held the match and we both did the spilling
Half's got your name and half's got my name
Come on, baby, split the blame

[Bridge: half-time, softer, voices trading]
You were a good dad. You were a good mom.
We made one good thing
And she's walking across that lawn

[Final Chorus: key up a step, both voices, loudest]
So let's split the blame, right down the middle
I'll take the big half, you take the little
I wasn't a saint, you weren't a villain
We both held the match and we both did the spilling
Half's got your name and half's got my name
Come on, baby, split the blame

[Outro: guitar riff, spoken over it]
Dinner after?
You're buying.
Split it.
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 128 BPM, 4/4, A major, rising to B major for the last chorus. Bright, fast and good-humoured, like an argument both people are enjoying.

VOICE: A duet. Male voice: easy, slightly nasal, amused. Female voice: clear, dry, quicker than he is. They take a verse each, swap the pre-choruses and sing the choruses together in close harmony. Three spoken lines at the end.

INSTRUMENTS: A clean, chiming electric guitar riff, driving live drums with a big snare, picked bass, strummed acoustic guitar, handclaps in the chorus, a bright synth pad low in the mix, pedal steel answering in the bridge.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro riff. 0:08 Verse 1, him. 0:30 Pre-chorus, her. 0:38 Chorus 1. 1:02 Verse 2, her. 1:24 Pre-chorus, him. 1:32 Chorus 2. 1:56 Bridge, half-time. 2:16 Final chorus, key up. 2:44 Outro riff with three spoken lines, ends 3:12.

PRODUCTION & MIX: 2024 pop-country with a 1980s pop-rock shine: glossy, wide, punchy drums, both voices equally loud.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The bridge at 1:56, when the joking stops for three lines.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The original is two young men sharing out the blame for a fresh break-up. This is years later, between the two people involved, with a grown child in view and nothing left to win.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Sparring, owning up, one sincere moment, easy company.
